cases.description: Mention and tag rendering with configured URL templates.
Symbol shortcode rendering against a supplied map (e.g. emoji glyphs), plus name-shape and word-boundary literal cases.
Locale-specific smart quotes using German quote characters.
Bare URLs become links when autolinking is explicitly enabled.
Bracketed [@key] citations with numbered output and a references list.
Bracketed [@key] citations with author-date output and a sorted references list.
An undefined citation key renders as the verbatim source; defined keys still resolve.
A [@key]{.attr} bracket is a span, not a citation (tail disambiguation).
A semicolon inside a locator falls back to literal text (not a citation).
In-code <n> markers render as <b class="callout"> bubbles and the following <n> list binds as <ol class="callouts"> with explicit values.
A code block with no marker does not bind the following list; the <n> line stays a literal paragraph.
An in-code marker still renders its bubble when no callout list follows; the prose stays a literal paragraph.
A 'p.' locator sets data-locator-label=page and data-locator to the numeric value.
A 'pp.' locator with a range and trailing text splits into value and suffix.
Multiple locator labels (chap., §) parse to their canonical citeproc names.
A bare digit locator with no label defaults to data-locator-label=page.
A roman numeral locator with no label produces no data-locator-label; the value is a suffix.
Labels only match at a boundary; 'pageant' and 'voli' are not page/volume labels.
Text after the locator value (comma suffix) is captured as data-suffix.
A label with no numeric value still sets data-locator-label; inline suffix is captured.
A [+@key] group with leading '+' is wrapped in a span with data-cite-mode=integral.
'+' is a group-level flag (integral mode) not a per-item marker; per-item '+' is literal prefix text.
A '-' before @key in a non-integral group sets data-suppress-author per item.
A trailing comma with no locator ([@key,]) is ignored - the item is a normal citation, not verbatim text (carve#227).
The details summary renders the quoted title's inline markup (phrasing content).
The list-table caption renders the quoted title's inline markup (phrasing content).
The spoiler summary renders the quoted title's inline markup (phrasing content).
A tab's quoted title is content: it stays inside the panel as the admonition-title line while the [label] becomes the tab button.
With the optional document-global smartTypography switch set to false, the whole converted set stays as authored ASCII; escapes, code spans and heading ids are unchanged (carve#338).

On the Markdown target a symbol keeps its :name: source spelling: the map resolves for HTML only, so the output re-parses to the same symbol node. Smart punctuation in the same case still resolves to its glyph (PART 9 section 8), which is the contrast.
With the optional Markdown-renderer setting that emits the author source run instead of the glyph, quotes, dashes and the ellipsis stay as the ASCII that was typed (PART 9 section 8; carve#360).

With the optional HTML-renderer sections switch set to false, no <section> is emitted: each heading carries the id it would have hoisted, alongside its other attributes, and the blocks that would have been section children stay siblings. Ids, dedup, crossrefs and implicit heading references are unchanged, and a heading inside a container renders exactly as it does with the wrapper on (PART 9 section 13; carve#427).

The data-source-line render annotation is emitted AFTER the generated heading id, not merely after the author's attributes (PART 10 section 1). An engine that stamps the line at parse time carries it inside the authored run, where the generated-last rule alone would put the id behind it; carve-rs did exactly that until a test caught it (carve#427).
